summary: Rocket Lab's vertical integration and Neutron rocket target small satellite launch demand, but supply-chain fragility in engine components and launch-site concentration pose risks. Insider buying suggests confidence, but Neutron's success and market growth assumptions are unproven.

inputs.whyNeeded: Primary propulsion for Electron and Neutron rockets
inputs.fragility: Low fragility due to vertical integration, but relies on rare-earth magnets for pumps

inputs.concentration: Sourced from multiple suppliers, but specialized
inputs.fragility: Medium fragility; single-source for high-grade carbon fiber could delay production
Low fragility, but chip shortages could impact

inputs.whyNeeded: Electric pump-fed engines require high-strength magnets
inputs.fragility: High fragility; geopolitical risk and limited substitutes

chokepoints.why: Primary launch site; single point of failure for Electron launches
Only planned site for Neutron; delays or damage halt all Neutron launches
Critical for engine production; concentrated in China

customers.why: Primary demand for Electron launches; growing constellation market
Key institutional customers for dedicated launches and space systems
Potential future demand for Neutron cargo missions

supplyChain.geographic: Launch sites in New Zealand and Virginia; rare-earth magnets from China; carbon fiber from Japan/US; engine production in California
supplyChain.substitutes: Falcon 9 rideshare for small sats; Vega-C for medium lift; Blue Origin New Glenn if operational

bearCase: Neutron fails or is delayed beyond 2028, leaving RKLB with only Electron revenue.
Rare-earth magnet export ban from China halts engine production for 6+ months.
SpaceX introduces a dedicated small-sat launcher, crushing RKLB's market share.
Launch site accident at Wallops or New Zealand grounds operations for a year.

loadBearing.assumption: a1: Neutron first launch by 2027 with 80% success
loadBearing.breaksIf: Engine test failures or structural issues push launch to 2028+

loadBearing.assumption: a2: Small satellite demand grows 15% CAGR
loadBearing.breaksIf: Constellation buildout slows or LEO spectrum congestion reduces launches
SpaceX launches Falcon 9 at cost or introduces a Neutron competitor
Rare-earth magnet supply disrupted or carbon fiber shortage

loadBearing.assumption: a8: FAA licenses granted without delays
loadBearing.breaksIf: Regulatory review extends beyond 12 months due to safety concerns

gaps: No facts on Neutron engine test results or production milestones.
No facts on rare-earth magnet inventory or supplier contracts.
No facts on launch site redundancy or backup plans.
No facts on customer backlog for Neutron beyond Electron.
verifyThese: Check if RKLB has long-term rare-earth magnet supply agreements.
Verify Neutron engine Archimedes test campaign status and success rate.
Confirm FAA licensing timeline for Neutron at Wallops.

diminishingReturns: Stopped at rare-earth magnets and launch sites; deeper hops (e.g., rare-earth mining in China) do not change the investment picture as substitutes are limited and geopolitical risk is already captured.
